In After, A shows a decisions heading with count one and a single plain-language line naming the missing Monday order sheet, the three handwritten orders and the lack of proof on the intended data. B carries that identical line as a Summary bullet in the same single edit that replaces the Integration instruction, with the original Summary bullet, the Notes text and the double spaces intact and no Rework block. C keeps `Keep  both  spaces.` unchanged and puts the same line inside the appended Rework block, with no separate Summary. To keep this stable, keep the wording explicit that a stand-in record counts as a decision even when it is the only entry, that the disclosure sentence is reused verbatim across the list, the Summary and the Rework block, and that on the linked route it rides in the same body edit as the Integration replacement. One loose end: in C the disclosure sits as a bare bullet between `Dropped claims:` and `Verification:`; a fixed position or label for it inside Rework would make the placement less likely to drift outside the block.
